summary: Built the official-information backend for brief 2 (U-R6, U-R7, O-R8) with the fixed I2 / I7 interfaces. (1) U-R6 CAL FIRE history: new sources/calfire_history.py keeps an append-only JSON-lines log per incident (data/official/calfire/<UniqueId>.jsonl, outside the bundles, atomic rewrite + fcntl lock). It adds a line when CAL FIRE's Updated time or a value (acres, containment, active, final, extinguished) changes; the first line is the baseline, and an older cached copy is never appended, so the log cannot go backwards. Recording happens whenever the backend checks CAL FIRE: every live-list and year-list fetch in catalog.py (the list endpoints, the live loop's cycle and summary sync, get_summary, live-status counts) records active and already-tracked fires. A tracked fire that leaves the live list gets its next record from its year's list. Each /api/official/calfire call records its fire. GET /api/official/calfire returns CAL FIRE's current record, value changes ([old, new] with CAL FIRE's update time and Fire-3d's first-seen time), recording_since_ms, a verbatim agency list, the incident link and caveats. The caveats cover: past fires have only CAL FIRE's final record; recording starts at the first check; a record edited long after containment (Eaton, Aug 2026). (2) U-R7 NWS: new sources/nws.py goes through fire3d.http with the User-Agent 'Fire-3d/0.1 (research prototype)'; the optional FIRE3D_NWS_CONTACT is appended (sanitized) for NWS requests only. Live: one statewide /alerts/active?area=CA&event=Red Flag Warning,Fire Weather Watch request (cached 2 min) serves every fire; /zones/fire/{UGC} polygons are cached 30 days. Per incident, alerts whose zones meet the analysis area + 15 km get covers_reported_location and nearest_km from the full polygons; the map gets outlines simplified to about 100 m. Past dates (at_ms older than now - 6 h, or a historical fire) use the IEM archive: bypoint at the reported location and the analysis-area corners, then vtec_event.py and geojson/vtec_event.py, labelled archived. The phase comes from the archive's per-zone times (the upgraded/cancelled-watch quirk included). Wording and onset/end come from the zone's segment of the latest NWS statement issued by at_ms, so the times match the quoted text and never reveal later extensions. Failures are honest: NWS down gives 'unavailable', the archive down gives 'not_available_for_past_dates', and an empty NWS answer is never used for a past date. Without an incident the endpoint returns every current California alert (for U-R12). (3) O-R8: /api/incidents?mode=historical&year=YYYY works for any year (default stays 2025; the response says which year), and every list row gains bbox_lonlat (the analysis area of a ready bundle, else null). The current year's CAL FIRE list is refreshed every 30 min and overlaid with the fresher live-list records, so a 2026-season row of an active fire matches its live row. Also: new api/official.py router included in app.py; pydantic models in contracts.py (IncidentListRow, CalFireOfficialResponse, FireWeatherResponse); SPEC §2 rows (NWS, IEM) and §6 rows plus TS shapes; CONTRACT §13 'official-backend' sub-heading. Offline tests use recorded and trimmed real samples.

verification: Backend gate: cd backend && uv run pytest -q -> 597 passed (549 before; new: test_official_nws.py 21, test_official_calfire.py 15, test_official_real_bundles.py 10 = every ready bundle in data/incidents with upstreams blocked, test_api.py +2; 48 new). The tests cover: VTEC/UGC parsing; verbatim CAP normalization; the real-statement segment parser; per-time statement choice; the upgraded-watch phase; the Eaton archive end to end (FW.W #1 in effect, FW.A #1 upcoming, FW.W/A #2 not yet issued, ended alerts kept 48 h); partial and total archive failures; live placement (covers/nearest, unplaced alerts listed with nulls, never dropped); endpoint states (past fire without at_ms -> past_date, archive down -> not_available_for_past_dates, NWS down -> unavailable, 400/404/422/429); User-Agent and Accept headers; history rules (baseline, Updated-only lines, stale copies, scope, concurrent writers, a fire leaving the live list, the live loop's cycle and summary sync); the current-year overlay; and every response validated strictly against contracts.py. A check showed tests never write to the real data/official. Web gates (no web files changed by me): npm run typecheck exit 0; npm run lint exit 0 with 57 warnings (the 55-warning src/scene baseline plus 2 in other agents' in-progress files: location/locationCheck.ts:63 unused 'address', App.tsx:75 set-state-in-effect); npm test 39 files / 555 tests passed; npm run build exit 0. Live smoke on :8714 with FIRE3D_LIVE=0 (all answers contract-valid): (a) GET /api/official/calfire for Henderson -> available, CAL FIRE 3,160 ac, 65% contained, active, CAL FIRE updated 2026-10-18 15:01 UTC, baseline recording_since 16:37:46 UTC, changes [] (nothing changed since recording began); Cooley -> 731.4 ac, 5%, updated 14:12 UTC, baseline 16:37:46 UTC. Eaton (past) -> final record 14,021 ac, 100%, and both past-fire caveats. (b) GET /api/official/fire-weather?incident=2026-henderson-fire-3e3dfe -> available, 0 alerts (NWS updated 16:45 UTC), caveats 'not an all-clear' and 'not an evacuation order'. (c) ...incident=2025-eaton-fire-dbfa57&at_ms=1736366400000 (Jan 8 2025 12:00 PST) -> source 'NWS products, archived copy: Iowa Environmental Mesonet'. 2025-KLOX-FW-W-0001 Red Flag Warning in_effect, covers the reported location (0 km), Jan 7 04:00 PST until Jan 9 18:00 PST, as stated in the Jan 7 14:37 PST statement whose verbatim headline is shown. Plus 2025-KLOX-FW-A-0001 Fire Weather Watch upcoming, Jan 9 18:00 to Jan 10 17:00 PST, with its own headline. 10 zone outlines, 25 KB. (d) GET /api/incidents?mode=historical&year=2026 -> 83 rows, 5 active, 3 with bbox_lonlat (Henderson, Cooley, Norte); active rows equal their live rows' CAL FIRE values. Default historical -> year 2025, 78 rows, 5 with bbox (unchanged count). Live -> 8 rows, 3 with bbox. (e) Count-only secret scan of backend/, SPEC.md, CONTRACT.md, the progress file, data/official and the smoke outputs: 181 files, 0 occurrences of the FIRMS key. No bundle was built and no build was triggered; the API was stopped afterwards and port 8714 is free.
contract_deviations: None against I2/I7's required fields. Additive fields (documented in CONTRACT 13 official-backend and SPEC §6): envelope kind, incident_id, caveats (both endpoints); source.license / terms_url; calfire current.extinguished_ms; alert phase ('upcoming'|'in_effect'|'ended'), office_url, nws_headline; fire-weather area_bbox and reported_location; /api/incidents 'year' on historical answers.

Interpretations I7 left open: calfire 'agencies' is CAL FIRE's AgencyNames string verbatim (free text), not a list. Alert 'url' is the NWS API record (JSON) for live alerts and IEM's event page for archived ones; office_url is the human-readable NWS office page. Archived alerts have message_type null and expires_ms null (no CAP message expiry). Their onset/ends are as stated by the latest statement by at_ms (the archive's per-zone times drive phase, and give ends once an alert ended).

Year lists keep row mode 'historical' (like the 2025 list always did) even for fires CAL FIRE still lists as active; is_active carries the status and /api/incidents/{id} resolves them as live. Shell's overview already merges live ∪ season with the live row winning.
CAL FIRE unreachable: status 'unavailable' still carries the last recorded current/changes (with the reason 'Showing the last record Fire-3d saw') rather than empty data.
app.py gained an import line besides the single include line (the import is required).
known_issues: CAL FIRE history starts on 2026-10-18; earlier changes are gone (e.g. Henderson's earlier 20% / 50% records are not in its history; its baseline is today's 65%). Past fires show only CAL FIRE's final record, as caveated.

data/official/calfire/ already holds real history written since 12:37 EDT by other agents' dev servers that import the new catalog hook (intended runtime behavior; data/ is gitignored). Cleanup scripts must not delete it.
Archive search samples 5 points (reported location + analysis-area corners); an alert covering only another part of the area could be missed. The caveat says what was searched.
IEM bypoint lists events by their start date; the window looks back 14 days, so a warning that began more than about 13 days earlier would be missed (none known in California).

Zone outlines in the response are simplified (~100 m; ~400 m statewide); a client point-in-zone test within about 100 m of a zone edge can differ from covers_reported_location, which uses the full NWS polygons.
Live NWS: ended alerts are only returned while NWS still lists them (official-web keeps seen alerts 48 h in the session). The archive keeps them 48 h after the end.

NWS publishes no rate limit; Fire-3d limits itself to 30 requests/min. On a cold start with many statewide alerts some zone outlines can be deferred: those alerts are listed with null distance plus a caveat.
If CAL FIRE ever moved a record's Updated time backwards, the new values would not be recorded until Updated passes the last line (the guard that blocks stale cached copies).
Screenshots are of a rendered evidence page of the API answers, not of the app: this role has only an API port. The UI that consumes these endpoints belongs to official-web / shell.
Lint at my run had 2 warnings outside src/scene in other agents' in-progress files (location/locationCheck.ts:63, App.tsx:75); none from this role.
notes_for_integrator: 1) Web API client (shell owns web/src/api/**): getIncidents must send year=2026 for the season list and year=2025 for the past list (CONTRACT 13 shell already says so). Type the rows as IncidentSummary & { bbox_lonlat: [w,s,e,n] | null } and the response's optional year: number. Season rows have mode 'historical'; use is_active, and let the live row win when merging. 2) official-web: build against the as-built shapes in CONTRACT 13 'official-backend' / SPEC §6. (a) Alert phase is 'upcoming' | 'in_effect' | 'ended'; map ended + vtec.action CAN/UPG to cancelled/replaced, other ended to expired. (b) Live alert ids are per CAP message: group by vtec office+phenomena+significance+etn. (c) Archived expires_ms is null: use ends_ms for 'until'. (d) 'headline' is the event's own headline; 'nws_headline' is the full NWS paragraph. (e) For a historical fire always pass at_ms, otherwise the answer is not_available_for_past_dates/past_date. (f) /api/official/fire-weather without incident gives statewide current alerts for U-R12. (g) calfire changes rows should use updated_ms (CAL FIRE's time) as the row time and seen_ms only as 'checked'. 3) README (not mine), please add: (a) GET /api/official/calfire and /api/official/fire-weather; (b) data/official/calfire/ (CAL FIRE history, outside the bundles; keep it when cleaning data/); (c) the optional env var FIRE3D_NWS_CONTACT (a website or email added to the NWS User-Agent; unset = anonymous); (d) credits in 'Data sources, licenses and credits': 'National Weather Service' (public domain/open data) and 'NWS products, archived copy via the Iowa Environmental Mesonet (Iowa State University)' (public domain, not an official NWS source). 4) Live loop (FIRE3D_LIVE=1): history is recorded every 15-min cycle through catalog.get_catalog('live', refresh=True) and the summary sync; nothing else to wire. 5) Quick checks: curl 'localhost:<api>/api/official/fire-weather?incident=2025-eaton-fire-dbfa57&at_ms=1736366400000' -> 2025-KLOX-FW-W-0001 in_effect; curl 'localhost:<api>/api/incidents?mode=historical&year=2026' -> about 83 rows. IEM answers for Eaton are cached 30 days in data/cache/http.
